titel: Bernard Gui's manual: the sect of the Beguins
autor: Bernard Gui (c. 1261–1331), Dominican, inquisitor of Toulouse 1307–1324, then bishop of Lodève
quelle: Practica inquisitionis heretice pravitatis auctore Bernardo Guidonis, ed. C. Douais (Paris: Alphonse Picard, 1886), part V, ch. IV, pp. 264–278. Internet Archive, practicainquisit00bern (University of Toronto, Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies). Public domain.
hinweis: Douais edited the manual from the Toulouse manuscript; his text is kept with its medieval spelling and his restorations in brackets, without the manuscript folio marks. The OCR of this printing is good, and each excerpt was read against the page images. Eleven excerpts from the chapter on the Beguins; the chapter goes on with their teaching on the Antichrist and the carnal Church, and with further questions, not carried here; cuts are marked […]. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: The inquisitor of Toulouse describes the lay followers of Olivi as he found them in court: their origins and their burnings since 1317, Olivi read in the vernacular, their houses of poverty and their greeting, the articles on Christ's poverty and the pope's power, the four friars of Marseille venerated as martyrs, the relics of the burned, and the questions to put to them.

units.titel: The sect of the Poor Brothers
units.orig: Bequinorum secta, qui Fratres Pauperes se appellant et dicunt se tenere et profiteri terciam regulam Sancti Francisci, modernis temporibus exsurrexit in provincia Provincie et in provincia Narbonensi. Ceperunt autem manifestari et detegi in suis opinionibus erroneis circa annum Domini M. CCC. XV., paulo plus minusve, quamvis prius suspecti communiter a pluribus haberentur; fueruntque postmodum successivis annis in provincia Narbonensi, et Tholosana, et in Cathalonia, plures capti, et detenti, et deprehensi in erroribus, et plures utriusque sexus inventi sunt et judicati heretici et combusti, ab anno Domini M CCC XVII citra, maxime Narbone, Biterris, et in dyocesi Agathensi, et in Lodova, et apud Lunellum Magalonensis dyocesis, et in Carcassona, et Tholose tres alienigene.
units.en: The sect of the Beguins, who call themselves Poor Brothers and say that they hold and profess the third rule of Saint Francis, arose in modern times in the province of Provence and in the province of Narbonne. They began to be revealed and uncovered in their erroneous opinions around the year of the Lord 1315, a little more or less, although before that they were commonly held suspect by many; and afterwards, in the following years, in the province of Narbonne, and of Toulouse, and in Catalonia, many were seized, and held, and caught in their errors, and many of both sexes were found and judged heretics and burned, from the year of the Lord 1317 onwards, above all at Narbonne, Béziers, in the diocese of Agde, at Lodève, at Lunel in the diocese of Maguelonne, at Carcassonne, and at Toulouse three foreigners.
units.note: The chapter heading 'De secta Bequinorum' is Douais's, not the manuscript's. Beguins here are lay men and women of the Franciscan third order in Languedoc, followers of Olivi and friends of the Spirituals; they are not the Beguines of the Low Countries. 'Three foreigners at Toulouse': Beguins from outside the diocese, such as Pierre Dominici of Narbonne and Pierre Hospitalis of Montpellier, whom Gui himself handed over at the sermon of 12 September 1322 (Sent. Dominici [1], Sent. Hospitalis [1]). Gui, who wrote this, became bishop of Lodève, one of the towns on the list, in 1324.

units.orig: Bequini igitur utriusque sexus moderni temporis sic vulgariter appellati, qui se dicunt Fratres Pauperes de penitentia de tercio ordine Sancti Francisci, portantes brunum seu de burello habitum cum mantello, et aliqui sine mantello, manifeste deprehensi sunt et confessi in juditio in diversis locis in provincia Narbonensi et in aliquibus locis provincie Tholosane, ab anno Domini M. CCC. XVII. ac deinceps successive, habere et tenere plures errores ac opiniones erroneas, extollentes se adversus Romanam Ecclesiam et apostolicam sedem, ac contra primatum sedis ejusdem et contra apostolicam potestatem domini pape ac prelatorum Ecclesie Romane. Inventum est autem per inquisitionem legitimam ac per depositiones et confessiones plurium ex ipsis, receptas in juditio, necnon per assertiones multorum ex ipsis, in quibus et pro quibus elegerunt mori pocius et comburi quam ab eis requisiti canonice resilire, quod errores suos et opiniones hujusmodi pestiferas ipsi habuerunt et collegerunt partim quidem ex libris seu opusculis fratris Petri Johannis Olivi qui fuit oriundus de Serinhano prope Bitterim, videlicet ex postilla ejusdem super Apocalipsim quam habent tam in latino quam etiam transpositam in vulgari; item ex aliquibus tractatibus quos ipsum fecisse Bequini dicunt et credunt, unum videlicet de paupertate et alium de mendicitate, et quemdam alium de dispensationibus, et ex quibusdam etiam aliis scriptitatis que sibi attribuunt, et que omnia habent in vulgari transposita, et ea legunt et eis credunt et intendunt tanquam scripturis autenticis; et dicunt et credunt dictum fratrem Petrum Johannis habuisse scientiam per revelationem factam sibi a Deo, specialiter in postilla seu expositione ejusdem super Apocalipsim; [...]
units.en: The Beguins of both sexes of modern times, then, so called in the vernacular, who call themselves Poor Brothers of penance of the third order of Saint Francis, wearing a brown habit, or one of coarse wool, with a cloak, and some without a cloak, have been plainly caught and have confessed in court, in various places in the province of Narbonne and in some places of the province of Toulouse, from the year of the Lord 1317 onwards, to having and holding many errors and erroneous opinions, raising themselves up against the Roman Church and the apostolic see, against the primacy of that see and against the apostolic power of the lord pope and of the prelates of the Roman Church. It has been found by lawful inquisition, and by the depositions and confessions of many of them received in court, and also by the assertions of many of them, in which and for which they chose rather to die and be burned than to withdraw from them when canonically required, that they took and gathered these errors and pestilent opinions partly from the books or little works of Brother Peter John Olivi, who was born at Sérignan near Béziers, namely from his postill on the Apocalypse, which they have in Latin and also translated into the vernacular; also from some treatises which the Beguins say and believe he made, one on poverty, another on begging, and another on dispensations, and from certain other writings which they attribute to him; all of which they have translated into the vernacular, and read, and believe and attend to as authentic scriptures; and they say and believe that the said Brother Peter John had his knowledge by a revelation made to him by God, especially in his postill or exposition on the Apocalypse; [...]
units.note: Peter John Olivi (d. 1298), the Franciscan theologian of Languedoc, whose tomb at Narbonne was venerated until the friars broke it up. Gui's list of his writings, in Latin and in Occitan translation, is the inquisitor's picture of a lay readership of theology. Eight masters examined the postill at Avignon in 1319, as Gui says a few lines further on; John XXII condemned it formally in 1326.

units.orig: Advertendum tamen est et notandum quod inter predictos Bequinos inveniuntur et sunt aliqui qui de infra scriptis erroribus plures aut omnes sciunt, tenent et credunt sicut magis imbuti fuerunt in eis et amplius indurati; alii vero sunt qui pautiores sciunt dicere ex eisdem et tamen quandoque pejores inveniuntur in adherentia et credentia errancium aliorum; aliqui vero sunt qui pauciores audierunt, aut retinuerunt, et acquiescunt rationi legitime et consilio saniori; quidam vero sunt qui obstinate persistunt et resilire nolunt, quin pocius mori preelegerunt quam eos abjurare, dicentes se in hoc defendere evangelicam veritatem et vitam Christi et evangelicam et apostolicam paupertatem; quidam autem ex eis inveniuntur et sunt qui in erroribus seu opinionibus erroneis implicari noluerunt et ab eis se custodiunt.
units.en: It must be observed and noted, however, that among the said Beguins there are some who know, hold and believe many or all of the errors written below, as those more steeped in them and more hardened; others who can tell fewer of them and yet are sometimes found worse in adhering to and believing others who err; some who have heard or kept fewer, and yield to lawful reason and sounder counsel; some who persist obstinately and will not withdraw, but have chosen rather to die than to abjure them, saying that in this they defend the truth of the gospel and the life of Christ and the poverty of the gospel and the apostles; and some of them are found who have refused to be entangled in the errors or erroneous opinions and keep themselves from them.
units.note: The inquisitor's typology, from the hardened to the innocent: the manual exists to tell them apart. Gui's sentence of 12 September 1322 describes two of the condemned in the same terms: they chose 'rather to die' in their errors 'than be converted' (Sent. Hospitalis [4]).

units.orig: Bequini itaque predicti habitantes in villis et castris habent mansiunculas in quibus aliqui simul cohabitant et eas appellant domos paupertatis tali suo vocabulo usitato, in quibus domibus tam ipsi cohabitantes quam etiam alii qui privatim in domibus suis manent, quam etiam familiares et amici Bequinorum, in diebus festis et in dominicis sepius conveniunt in unum, et ibi legunt aut legi audiunt in vulgari de predictis libellis aut opusculis ex quibus suggunt venenum, quamvis etiam quedam alia legantur ibidem de preceptis et de articulis fidei et de legendis sanctorum, et de Summa de viciis et virtutibus, ut sic schola dyaboli sub specie boni videatur scholam Christi, more symie, in aliquo imitari, cum precepta Dei et articuli fidei in sancta Ecclesia per rectores et pastores Ecclesie et doctores ac predicatores verbi Dei, non per laycos simplices, publice et non in clamculo, predicari debeant et exponi. Notandum quoque est quod inter eos sunt aliqui qui publice mendicant hostiatim, quia, ut dicunt, noverunt evangelicam paupertatem. Sunt et alii qui non mendicant publice, set aliqua suis manibus operantur et lucrantur, et pauperem vitam ducunt. Sunt autem quidam ex eis utriusque sexus simpliciores qui articulos seu errores infra scriptos explicite nesciunt, set ignorant; verumptamen nonnulli ex ipsis communiter credunt explicite quod fuit indebita et injusta condempnatio Bequinorum, que fuit facta in pluribus locis in provincia Narbonensi, videlicet Narbone et in Capitestagno, et Biterris, et apud Lodovam, et in dyocesi Agathensi, et apud Lunellum dyocesis Magalonensis, et in Massilia, et in Cathalonia, per juditium prelatorum et inquisitorum heretice pravitatis ab anno Domini M.CCC.XVIII. citra, et ipsos condempnatos tanquam hereticos reputant justos et bonos.
units.en: The said Beguins, then, living in towns and villages, have little dwellings in which some live together, and they call them houses of poverty, a word of their own in common use; in these houses, both those who live together and others who stay privately in their own houses, and also the intimates and friends of the Beguins, often gather on feast days and Sundays, and there they read, or hear read, in the vernacular from the said booklets or little works, from which they suck poison; although other things are also read there, on the commandments and the articles of faith, on the legends of the saints, and from the Summa of vices and virtues; so that the devil's school, under the appearance of good, seems to imitate the school of Christ in some way, as an ape does, whereas the commandments of God and the articles of faith ought to be preached and expounded in holy Church by the rectors and pastors of the Church and the doctors and preachers of the word of God, not by simple laymen, and in public and not in secret. It is also to be noted that among them there are some who beg publicly from door to door because, as they say, they have taken up gospel poverty. There are others who do not beg publicly, but work and earn something with their own hands and lead a poor life. There are, however, some of them, of both sexes, simpler folk, who do not know the articles or errors written below explicitly, but are ignorant of them; yet some of these commonly believe explicitly that the condemnation of the Beguins was undue and unjust which was carried out in many places in the province of Narbonne, namely at Narbonne and Capestang, Béziers, Lodève, the diocese of Agde, Lunel in the diocese of Maguelonne, and at Marseille and in Catalonia, by the judgment of prelates and inquisitors of heretical depravity from the year of the Lord 1318 onwards, and they hold those condemned as heretics to be just and good men.
units.note: The 'Summa of vices and virtues' is one of the standard handbooks of moral instruction, here read in the vernacular. 'Not by simple laymen': what the inquisitor objects to is less the content of the reading than who reads, where, and in what language. Believing that the burned were just men was itself a matter for the inquisitor's questions.

units.orig: Notandum est etiam quod, juxta illud quod ait Augustinus, Contra Faustum, libro XIX, dicens: In nullum nomen religionis seu verum seu falsum coagulari homines possunt nisi aliquo signaculorum vel sacramentorum visibilium consortio colligentur; ideoque Bequini hujusmodi quedam specialia observant et habent exterius in modo conversandi ex quibus possunt discerni a ceteris tam in loquendo quam etiam in aliis. Modus enim salutandi ipsorum aut resalutandi talis est: dicunt enim venientes aut intrantes domum aliquam aut occurrentes sibi ipsis in itinere seu in via: Benedictus sit Jhesus Christus, vel: Benedictum sit nomen Domini Jhesu Christi. Item, orantes in ecclesia vel alibi sedent acrupiti, verso vultu seu facie communiter ad objectum parietem vel similem locum, vel ad terram capuciati, et raro videntur stare flexis genibus et complosis manibus sicut faciunt ceteri homines. Item, in mensa in prandio post benedictionem mense dicunt illi qui sciunt Gloria in excelsis Deo, flexis genibus, ceteris audientibus. In cena vero dicunt Salve, Regina illi qui sciunt, similiter flexis genibus.
units.en: It is to be noted also that, according to what Augustine says in book XIX Against Faustus, 'men cannot be bound together under any name of religion, true or false, unless they are joined by some fellowship of visible signs or sacraments'; and so Beguins of this kind keep and have certain special outward marks in their manner of life by which they can be told from others, in speech as well as in other things. Their way of greeting, or of returning a greeting, is this: when they come to or enter a house, or meet one another on a journey or in the road, they say 'Blessed be Jesus Christ', or 'Blessed be the name of the Lord Jesus Christ'. Also, when they pray in church or elsewhere, they sit crouched, commonly with their face turned to a wall facing them or some such place, or hooded towards the ground, and are seldom seen to stand kneeling with joined hands as other people do. Also, at table at the midday meal, after the blessing of the table, those who know it say the Gloria in excelsis Deo on their knees, the others listening. At supper those who know it say the Salve Regina, likewise on their knees.
units.note: Nothing in these signs is heretical; they are listed because an inquisitor recognises a sect by its habits before he hears its doctrine. The Salve Regina and the Gloria were ordinary Catholic prayers.

units.orig: In primis itaque dicunt et asserunt illi qui a vulgo Bequini nominantur, ipsi autem se dicunt Fratres Pauperes de penitentia de tercio ordine Sancti Francisci, se credere et tenere quod Dominus Jhesus Christus in quantum fuit homo et ejus apostoli nichil habuerunt in proprio nec etiam in communi, quia fuerunt perfecti pauperes in hoc mundo. Item, hanc dicunt esse perfectam evangelicam paupertatem, videlicet nichil habere in proprio nec in communi. Item, dicunt quod habere aliquid in communi diminuit de perfectione evangelice paupertatis. Item, quod apostoli sine diminutione perfectionis eorum et sine peccato non potuerunt habere aliquid nec in proprio nec in communi. Item, dicunt esse hereticum credere et asserere contrarium predictorum. Item, dicunt quod Regula Sancti Francisci est illa vita Jhesu Christi quam Christus servavit in hoc mundo et quam apostolis suis tradidit et imposuit observandam. Item, quod sanctus Franciscus tradidit fratribus sui ordinis in regula sua supra dictam evangelicam paupertatem, ita quod professores dicte regule nichil possunt habere nec in proprio nec in communi preter usum pauperem necessarium ad vitam, qui semper sapiat indigentiam paupertatis nichilque habeat superfluum.
units.en: First, then, those whom the common people call Beguins, while they call themselves Poor Brothers of penance of the third order of Saint Francis, say and assert that they believe and hold that the Lord Jesus Christ, in so far as he was man, and his apostles had nothing individually, nor even in common, because they were perfectly poor in this world. Also, they say that this is perfect gospel poverty, namely to have nothing individually nor in common. Also, they say that to have something in common diminishes the perfection of gospel poverty. Also, that the apostles could not, without diminishing their perfection and without sin, have anything either individually or in common. Also, they say that it is heretical to believe and assert the contrary of these things. Also, they say that the rule of Saint Francis is that life of Jesus Christ which Christ kept in this world and handed on to his apostles and laid on them to observe. Also, that Saint Francis handed on to the brothers of his order in his rule the gospel poverty described above, so that the professors of that rule can have nothing, individually or in common, except the poor use necessary for life, which must always savour of the want of poverty and have nothing superfluous.
units.note: The first article is the sentence John XXII declared heretical in November 1323 (Decr. Nonnullos [1]); the Beguins add that its contrary is the heresy. 'Poor use' (usus pauper) is Olivi's doctrine, which Clement V had half conceded at Vienne (Exivi [4]).

units.orig: Item, predictam Regulam Sancti Francisci dicunt esse Evangelium Christi aut unum et idem esse cum Evangelio Christi. Item, dicunt quod quicumque impugnant vel contradicunt in aliquo Regule Sancti Francisci quam dicunt esse Evangelium impugnant et contradicunt Evangelio Christi, et per consequens errant et fiunt heretici si in hoc perseverent. Item, dicunt quod sicut papa aut aliquis alius non potest aliquid immutare in Evangelio Christi nec addere, nec subtrahere ex eodem, ita non potest aliquid immutare in predicta Regula Sancti Francisci, nec addere nec subtrahere ex eadem quantum ad vota, seu consilia evangelica, aut precepta contenta in ipsa. [...] Item, dicunt quod papa, nec etiam generale concilium, non potest cassare aut statuere contrarium alicujus illorum que per predecessorem suum papam vel precedens concilium generale fuerunt confirmata statuta vel etiam ordinata [...]. Item, dicunt quod si papa immutaret aliquid in Regula Sancti Francisci vel adderet, aut subtraheret ex eadem, precipue quantum ad votum paupertatis, aut si dictam Regulam cassaret, in hoc faceret contra Evangelium Christi, nec aliquis frater Minor aut aliquis alius teneretur obedire eidem in predictis, quantumcumque preciperet alicui aut etiam excommunicaret non obedientem sibi, quia talis excommunicatio esset injusta et aliquem non ligaret.
units.en: Also, they say that the said rule of Saint Francis is the Gospel of Christ, or one and the same with the Gospel of Christ. Also, they say that whoever attacks or contradicts the rule of Saint Francis in anything, which they say is the Gospel, attacks and contradicts the Gospel of Christ, and consequently errs and becomes a heretic if he persists in this. Also, they say that as the pope or anyone else cannot change anything in the Gospel of Christ, nor add to it nor take anything from it, so he cannot change anything in the said rule of Saint Francis, nor add to it nor take from it, as to the vows or the gospel counsels or the precepts contained in it. [...] Also, they say that the pope, nor even a general council, cannot annul, or ordain the contrary of, any of the things that were confirmed, enacted or even ordained by his predecessor as pope or by a previous general council [...]. Also, they say that if the pope changed anything in the rule of Saint Francis, or added to it or took from it, especially as to the vow of poverty, or if he annulled the rule, he would in this act against the Gospel of Christ, and no Friar Minor or anyone else would be bound to obey him in these things, however much he commanded someone, or even excommunicated whoever did not obey him, because such an excommunication would be unjust and would not bind anyone.
units.note: The lay form of the argument the friars at Louis's court would make in 1324 (Sachs. Poverty [5]) and Ockham after them (OND [6]): what one pope has confirmed, no successor may undo. In the mouths of Beguins in Languedoc it went to the stake.

units.titel: Granaries, and a pope who is no longer pope
units.orig: Item, dicunt quod papa non potest facere constitutionem decretalem per quam dispenset aut concedat Fratribus Minoribus quod possint habere bladum et vinum ad servandum in communi in granariis vel cellariis pro tempore futuro ad suum usum seu victum necessarium, quia hoc esset facere contra evangelicam Regulam Sancti Francisci et per consequens contra Evangelium Christi. Item, dicunt quod dominus papa Johannes XXIIus faciendo quamdam constitutionem que incipit: Quorumdam, in qua dicitur concedere aut dispensare cum Fratribus Minoribus quod possint congregare bladum et vinum in granariis vel cellariis pro tempore futuro, ad arbitrium prelatorum ordinis ipsorum, fecit contra evangelicam paupertatem et per consequens, ut aiunt, contra Evangelium Christi; et ideo dicunt quod factus est hereticus et quod ex hoc perdidit potestatem papalem ligandi et solvendi et alia faciendi si in hoc perseverat, et quod prelati per eum facti ex quo dictam constitutionem fecit non habent aliquam ecclesiasticam jurisdictionem seu potestatem. Item, quod omnes prelati et alii qui eidem domino pape in dicta constitutione facienda consenserunt aut consentiunt scienter, ex hoc facti sunt heretici si in hoc pertinaciter perseverent, et quod omnem potestatem seu jurisdictionem ecclesiasticam perdiderunt. Item, dicunt quod Fratres Minores qui dictam constitutionem fieri procurarunt, aut qui eidem consentiunt, et eam recipiunt, vel ea utuntur, ex hoc heretici sunt effecti.
units.en: Also, they say that the pope cannot make a decretal constitution by which he dispenses or grants the Friars Minor that they may have grain and wine to keep in common in granaries or cellars for the future, for their use or necessary food, because this would be to act against the gospel rule of Saint Francis and consequently against the Gospel of Christ. Also, they say that the lord pope John XXII, by making a certain constitution which begins Quorumdam, in which he is said to grant or dispense the Friars Minor that they may gather grain and wine in granaries or cellars for the future, at the discretion of the prelates of their order, acted against gospel poverty and consequently, as they say, against the Gospel of Christ; and therefore they say that he has become a heretic and has thereby lost the papal power of binding and loosing and of doing other things, if he persists in this, and that the prelates made by him since he made that constitution have no ecclesiastical jurisdiction or power. Also, that all prelates and others who consented or knowingly consent to the lord pope in making that constitution have thereby become heretics, if they persist in this pertinaciously, and have lost all ecclesiastical power or jurisdiction. Also, they say that the Friars Minor who procured the making of that constitution, or who consent to it, and receive it, or use it, have thereby become heretics.
units.note: Quorumdam exigit (7 October 1317) put the granaries and cellars at the discretion of the order's superiors (Decr. Exigit [4]); the Spirituals of Languedoc had complained of them since before Vienne (Exivi [3]). For the Beguins the dispute over Christ's poverty began not in 1322 but here, with the grain and the wine: a pope who allowed a store for the future had broken the Gospel and ceased to be pope.

units.orig: Item, dicunt quod illi quatuor fratres Minores qui sub anno Domini M. CCC. XVIII. apud Massiliam per inquisitorem heretice pravitatis, qui etiam erat de ordine Fratrum Minorum, fuerunt velut heretici condempnati ex hoc ut ipsi dicunt, quia volebant servare et tenere puritatem et veritatem et paupertatem dicte Regule Sancti Francisci, et quia nolebant consentire in laxationem regule, nec recipere dispensationem predicti domini pape factam super illa, nec sibi nec aliis super hoc obedire, fuerunt condempnati injuste pro veritate regule evangelice defendenda; et ideo dicunt ipsos non fuisse hereticos, set catholicos et esse martires gloriosos, ipsorumque implorant orationes et suffragia apud Deum. Item, multi ex eis dicunt se credere eos esse non minoris meriti apud Deum quam sanctos Laurentium et Vincentium martires. Item, quidam ex ipsis dicunt quod in ipsis IIIIor fratribus Minoribus fuit Christus iterum spiritualiter crucifixus tanquam in IIIIor brachiis crucis, et paupertas Christi et vita ejus fuit in ipsis condempnata. Item, dicunt quod si prefatus dominus papa mandavit aut consentiit, aut consentit quod predicti IIIIor fratres Minores fuerint per inquisitorem velut heretici condempnati, ex hoc ipse factus est hereticus et major etiam inter alios, cum deberet ipse sicut caput Ecclesie perfectionem evangelicam defendere, et ideo, ut dicunt, papalem perdidit potestatem nec eum credunt esse papam et quod non est ei obediendum in aliquo a fidelibus, et quod ex tunc vacavit papatus.
units.en: Also, they say that those four Friars Minor who in the year of the Lord 1318 were condemned as heretics at Marseille by the inquisitor of heretical depravity, who was himself of the order of Friars Minor, because, as they say, they wished to keep and hold the purity and truth and poverty of the said rule of Saint Francis, and because they would not consent to the relaxing of the rule, nor accept the dispensation the said lord pope had made concerning it, nor obey him or others in this, were unjustly condemned for defending the truth of the gospel rule; and therefore they say that they were not heretics but catholics, and are glorious martyrs, and they implore their prayers and intercession before God. Also, many of them say they believe them to be of no less merit before God than the holy martyrs Lawrence and Vincent. Also, some of them say that in those four Friars Minor Christ was spiritually crucified again, as on the four arms of the cross, and that the poverty of Christ and his life were condemned in them. Also, they say that if the said lord pope ordered or consented, or consents, that the said four Friars Minor were condemned as heretics by the inquisitor, he has thereby become a heretic, and the greatest among the others, since he as head of the Church ought to have defended gospel perfection; and therefore, as they say, he has lost the papal power, and they do not believe him to be pope, and hold that he is not to be obeyed by the faithful in anything, and that from that time the papacy has been vacant.
units.note: Jean Barrau, Déodat Michel, Guillaume Sainton and Pons Rocha, Spiritual friars, burned at Marseille on 7 May 1318 by the Franciscan inquisitor Michel Lemoine for refusing to obey Quorundam exigit. Pierre Dominici's sentence at Toulouse names the same belief among his errors (Sent. Dominici [3]).

units.orig: Item, multi Bequini et Bequine ac etiam credentes ipsorum recollegerunt occulte ossa combusta et cineres predictorum combustorum qui fuerunt velut heretici condempnati ad conservandum sibi pro reliquiis, et tanquam reliquias sanctorum osculabantur et venerabantur, sicut aliorum sanctorum, ob devotionem et reverentiam eorumdem, sicut compertum et inventum per inquisitionem et per confessiones ac depositiones quorumdam Bequinorum receptas in juditio qui talia secum habebant et alios habere et habuisse viderant et sciebant; sic quoque nos inquirentes de talibus reliquiis apud eos inventis palpavimus et vidimus et fide probavimus oculata. Item, aliqui ex Bequinis scripserunt et notaverunt nomina predictorum condempnatorum et dies seu kalendas in quibus passi fuerunt sicut martires, ut ipsi asserunt, secundum quod Ecclesia Dei de sanctis et justis martiribus facere consuevit, et nomina eorum annotaverunt in suis kalendariis et in suis invocabant letaniis.
units.en: Also, many Beguin men and women, and also their believers, secretly gathered the burned bones and the ashes of those burned, who had been condemned as heretics, to keep them as relics, and kissed and venerated them as the relics of saints, like those of other saints, out of devotion and reverence for them, as has been discovered and found by inquisition and by the confessions and depositions, received in court, of certain Beguins who had such things with them and had seen and knew that others had and had had them; and we too, inquiring, have handled and seen such relics found among them and proved it with the evidence of our own eyes. Also, some of the Beguins wrote down and noted the names of the said condemned and the days or kalends on which they suffered as martyrs, as they assert, in the way the Church of God is accustomed to do for holy and just martyrs, and they entered their names in their calendars and invoked them in their litanies.
units.note: The inquisitor's one sentence in the first person plural: he has held the bones himself. The Beguins' own list, a litany of about seventy names read aloud before Gui, is recorded in the Book of Sentences without the names (Sent. Dominici [5]); the game Nec in communi can name only those whose names the sentences keep.

units.orig: Est autem sciendum et advertendum quod quidam ex ipsis Bequinis plura de predictis articulis erroneis et erroribus didiscerunt et sciunt, et alii pauciora, sicut magis et minus eruditi seu imbuti sunt in eisdem, ut moris est in talibus semper in pejus proficere successive, nec simul omnia tradere set paulatim; unde inquirendo sollers inquisitor interrogare poterit aut de omnibus, vel singulis, aut de aliquibus tantum, aliis pretermissis, prout expediens esse viderit et qualitas seu condicio personarum que examinande fuerint et natura officii inquisitionis exegerit; [...] quin ex interrogationibus convenienter propositis et ex responsionibus factis veritas subtilius et facilius invenitur et dolus cicius deprehenditur, si non respondeant clare et proprie ad interrogata, querentes verborum velamina et occasiones subterfugiendi ne directe respondeant ad quesita, que omnia experientia magis docet. [...] Item, examinandus interrogetur si audivit aliquos docentes et asserentes quod Christus et apostoli nichil habuerint neque in proprio neque in communi. Item, si audivit dici quod tenere aut credere contrarium sit hereticum. Item, si audivit dogmatizari quod habere aliquid in communi diminuat de perfectione evangelice paupertatis. Item, si audivit dici aut dogmatizari, et si ipse credidit et credit, quod Regula Sancti Francisci sit unum et idem cum Evangelio Christi aut sit Evangelium Christi.
units.en: It is to be known and observed that some of these Beguins have learned and know more of the said erroneous articles and errors, and others fewer, according as they are more or less taught or steeped in them, since it is the way in such matters always to advance for the worse by degrees, and not to hand everything on at once but little by little; so in his inquiry a skilful inquisitor will be able to question them either on all points, or on each, or only on some, leaving others aside, as he sees fit and as the quality or condition of the persons to be examined and the nature of the office of inquisition require; [...] for from questions fittingly put and from the answers given the truth is found more subtly and more easily, and deceit is caught more quickly, if they do not answer clearly and properly to what they are asked, seeking veils of words and occasions of evasion so as not to answer the questions directly: all of which experience teaches best. [...] Also, let the one being examined be asked whether he has heard any teaching and asserting that Christ and the apostles had nothing, either individually or in common. Also, whether he has heard it said that to hold or believe the contrary is heretical. Also, whether he has heard it taught that to have something in common diminishes the perfection of gospel poverty. Also, whether he has heard it said or taught, and whether he himself believed and believes, that the rule of Saint Francis is one and the same with the Gospel of Christ, or is the Gospel of Christ.
units.note: The questions follow the articles one by one: the list of errors becomes a script for the interrogation. The first questions, left out here, ask when and by which minister the suspect was received into the third order, and whether the local bishop examined him in the faith, as John XXII had ordered. The articles confessed by Pierre Dominici and Pierre Hospitalis at Toulouse answer these questions point by point (Sent. Dominici [2], Sent. Hospitalis [2]).
